capability: Keep current-route firmware artifact classification and multi-capacity ambiguity resolution owned by Application
searchEvidence: Trace CompiledFirmwareArtifactClassifier, BuiltInFirmwareInspection, current capability publication, dynamic selection-group compilation, and every ArtifactClassification consumer across src and tests
Verify NT51928 exact 256 KiB and 512 KiB containers, shared TP prefix, unknown shape, conflicting multi-map shape, missing IC, and stale publication
Require Infrastructure to consume one terminal Application decision and prohibit filename, PID, hash, or iteration-order inference
semanticOwner: Application resolves current Standard Merge geometries and returns one terminal typed artifact classification; Infrastructure only supplies immutable accepted bytes and projects that result
terminalContract: An exact current capability or unique exact container capacity selects one compiled geometry. A TP-prefix result without exact capacity is returned only when every current geometry agrees; divergent, missing, stale, contract-mismatched, or incompletely enumerated candidates fail closed. Dynamic selection-group candidates must exactly cover the published allowed map set and classification remains independent from authoring availability.

designReview.evidence: The frozen-head R2 review found that lower-level signals were Application-owned but candidate route enumeration and FlashCode-over-TP ranking still lived in Infrastructure. It required Application-owned exact variant resolution, stale and ambiguity fail-closed behavior, and NT51928 dual-capacity evidence without a second executor or map implementation.
